g.title: OSREC
g.text: OSREC — current flow, responsibilities and underlying tools
Solid arrows: data / execution flow • Dashed arrows: workflow control

g.title: cluster_capture
g.text: 1 NATIVE CAPTURE + KERNEL SLICES

g.title: cluster_application
g.text: 2 APPLICATION IMPORT + COMPOSITION

g.title: cluster_guest
g.text: 3 FREESTANDING REPLAY RUNTIME

g.title: cluster_chain
g.text: 4 CHECKPOINTS + VERIFICATION

g.title: orchestrators
g.text: Select and run a replay workflow
QEMU + Clang/LLVM: record a native scenario and build replay
Native capture → port → slices → proof → test checkpoint chain
Clang + local gateway + QMP: compile C and advance checkpoints
C test frontend → import → shared stage engine
ELF loader + state codec + QMP: import or continue saved execution
Supplied ELF / checkpoint or --resume-checkpoint → shared stage engine

g.title: linux
g.text: Linux AArch64 native capture
QEMU AArch64: execute native SVC calls and record results
Native kernel boot binary: ARM64 Image + config
QEMU native SVC workload
Capture calls, raw returns, copied bytes, observed umask

g.title: orchestrators->linux
g.text: Native capture or existing observations

g.title: c
g.text: C application test frontend
TESTING PURPOSES: generate controlled application fixtures
Clang + LLD + LLVM symbols: compile and derive metadata
Application C + spec.json → application.elf + checkpoint.json
Derive entry / stack, SVC sites, exit boundary and assertions

g.title: orchestrators->c
g.text: Test application C, contract and pause positions

g.title: user
g.text: Supplied application checkpoint
Application ELF: static AArch64 user program
Neutral user-state JSON
CPU frame, memory overlays, objects, ordered SVC PCs

g.title: orchestrators->user
g.text: Application ELF and saved user state
or matching joint checkpoint

g.title: ohos
g.text: LiteOS-A test capture
TESTING PURPOSES: pinned kernel validation fixture
Kernel instrumentation + QEMU Cortex-A7: record syscall boundaries
Build / boot real ARMv7 kernel in QEMU
Instrumented syscall boundaries + independent user observations

g.title: port
g.text: Validate capture and prepare reviewed port
Reviewed adapters + JSON policies + SHA-256 identity checks
Linux external bundle or built-in OHOS file adapter
Kernel C: selected syscall/helpers + reviewed model C
port.json + checkpoint policy

g.title: linux->port
g.text: Native capture JSON + provenance
Calls / returns / bytes / initial state

g.title: ohos->port
g.text: Kernel + user observations
Entry state + ordered dependency events

g.title: context
g.text: Transform kernel state into per-session context
Clang resolves declarations; OSREC rewrites kernel C
Clang AST: mutable globals / local statics → context fields
References become ctx->field; callers pass ctx
Generate restoration helpers; ordinary locals stay on stack

g.title: port->context
g.text: Kernel C sources + reviewed model headers
Selected original bodies / reviewed dependencies

g.title: codec
g.text: Generate portable kernel checkpoint codec
Clang provides target layout; OSREC generates codec C
Reviewed policy covers every context field
Save scalar bytes and logical reference IDs / offsets
Load: reconstruct seeds → overlay saved values → rebind pointers

g.title: context->codec
g.text: Rewritten kernel C + slice_context.h
context-plan.json + reviewed field policy

g.title: archive
g.text: Build returning slices and proof image
Clang cross-compiler + LLVM archive builder + LLD linker
Clang / LLVM: AArch64 freestanding build + llvm-ar
Kernel library: slices.a
Kernel-slice proof: slices.elf / slices.bin + manifest.json

g.title: codec->archive
g.text: Generated runtime C: slice_codec.c + schema
Transformed closure / adapter / embedded capture

g.title: proof
g.text: Validate kernel proof image
QEMU Cortex-A53: compare ELF/raw runs from EL1 and EL3
QEMU: ELF / raw × EL1 / EL3
Compare 128-byte results; retain verification-matrix.json

g.title: archive->proof
g.text: Kernel-slice proof ELF / raw + manifest.json
Expected proof result / archive identity

g.title: compose
g.text: Compose self-contained replay image
Clang + LLD + LLVM utilities: link embedded code and state
Embed application payloads, slices.a, loader, gateway, state
Generated runtime C: loader / gateway / replay driver
Combined replay: slices.elf / slices.bin (app + kernel slices)

g.title: proof->compose
g.text: Verified kernel package: slices.a
Sources / initial state / codec / manifest

g.title: restore
g.text: Restore application and kernel state
AArch64 frame runtime: restore CPU registers and application RAM
Restore GPR / SIMD / FP / thread pointer / RAM
Initial kernel context or saved portable record

g.title: import
g.text: Validate and import application
ELF segment loader + instruction audit: validate and patch routes
Check ELF hash, PT_LOAD mapping, permissions and instructions
Patch declared SVCs → BRKs; deduplicate repeated PCs
Output application original.elf / patched.elf
RAM payloads + route-plan.json

g.title: c->import
g.text: Application ELF: application.elf + checkpoint.json
Derived CPU / memory / route metadata

g.title: user->import
g.text: Application ELF bytes + user-state JSON
Saved frame / RAM overlays / SVC history

g.title: import->compose
g.text: Application ELF: original.elf + patched.elf
RAM payloads / frame / route-plan.json

g.title: compose->restore
g.text: Combined replay ELF / raw image
Application bytes / frame / initial kernel state

g.title: freeze
g.text: Export joint checkpoint from stopped guest
QMP memory observation + checkpoint validation: package stopped state
QMP reads saved frame, RAM and kernel record externally
Output kernel.bin + checkpoint.json + application/ + manifest.json
Pin ordinal, completed-call history, generation and parent identity

g.title: verify
g.text: Verify each stage and publish evidence
QEMU execution matrix + artifact hashes: publish checked evidence
ELF / raw × EL1 / EL3; resumed intervals execute twice
Check result bytes, artifacts, state identity and checkpoint lineage
Output stage-N/{image,qemu,checkpoint}, finish/, workflow.json

g.title: compose->verify
g.text: Image + manifest + expected results
Combined replay ELF / raw + construction artifacts

g.title: el0
g.text: Execute application at EL0
Application prepares syscall arguments and consumes results
Kernel state persists across sequential calls

g.title: restore->el0
g.text: Restored PC / SP / GPR / SIMD / FP
User RAM + thread pointer

g.title: gateway
g.text: Route declared syscall locally
AArch64 BRK gateway: save the frame and dispatch calls
BRK exception → save frame / validate expected route
Linux: x8 number, x0–x5 arguments; port defines ABI

g.title: el0->gateway
g.text: BRK trap + live application frame
Syscall number / arguments / next ordinal

g.title: boundary
g.text: Declared pause or exit boundary
Pause before next call at selected absolute ordinal
Final exit checks kernel completion + application memory assertions

g.title: el0->boundary
g.text: Current CPU / RAM + syscall ordinal
Pause route or declared exit PC

g.title: syscall
g.text: Execute selected original syscall body
Returning slice/session runtime: execute code with reviewed models
Reviewed dependency models + restored context
Check supported arguments / ordered boundary events as contracted

g.title: gateway->syscall
g.text: Validated syscall invocation
Context pointer + arguments + user memory

g.title: return
g.text: Return to application
Result in x0; restore application frame
Resume at original SVC PC + 4

g.title: syscall->return
g.text: Computed return value + updated state
User-buffer writes / dependency progress

g.title: return->el0
g.text: x0 result + restored frame
PC = original SVC PC + 4; user writes retained

g.title: cheatsheet
g.text: Quick reference
Shared stage engine
Common host workflow for test-C and supplied-ELF inputs:
build each image, verify it, save state and continue.
QEMU
Emulates the target CPU and machine for native
capture and functional replay validation.
QMP
QEMU Machine Protocol: a host control channel used
to inspect stopped guest memory for checkpoint export.
Clang / AST
C compiler and typed Abstract Syntax Tree used to
identify declarations, types and state references.
LLVM / LLD
LLVM compiles code and supplies binary utilities.
LLD links selected code and state into the executable.
Context / codec
Context owns mutable session state. A codec saves
selected values and rebuilds references during restore.
ELF / PT_LOAD
Executable format and loadable segments describing
addresses, file bytes and zero-filled memory extents.
EL0 / EL1 / EL3
AArch64 privilege levels: app at EL0, gateway at EL1.
Verification also tests a more privileged EL3 start.
SVC / BRK
Native syscall instruction / local breakpoint trap.
Declared SVC sites become BRKs routed by the gateway.
Ordinal
Absolute completed-call count: identifies the next
syscall and the position at which replay resumes.

g.title: boundary->freeze
g.text: Paused frame + RAM + encoded kernel record
External QMP dumps in pause-records/

g.title: boundary->verify
g.text: Final result block + assertion status
Completion / model-transcript checks per port

g.title: resume
g.text: Compose fresh image / resume remaining interval
Clang/LLD + state codec: compose and restore a fresh image
Restore portable state; rebind context-owned references
Alternate container addresses to exercise relocation
Final suffix completes without another intermediate checkpoint

g.title: freeze->resume
g.text: Joint package: kernel.bin + application/
checkpoint.json / manifest / generation / parent hash

g.title: resume->restore
g.text: Fresh image + joint snapshot
Saved ordinal / values + rebound references

g.title: resume->verify
g.text: Resumed image + input checkpoint identity
Expected interval / state / assertions

g.title: offline
g.text: Offline verification of retained package
SHA-256 checks + route/lineage validation: verify retained evidence
Recheck hashes, routes, ordinals, generations and saved evidence
Original construction inputs are no longer required

g.title: verify->offline
g.text: workflow.json + matrix reports + hashes
Images / result bytes / checkpoint lineage

g.title: artifact_reference
g.text: C / ELF: which side?
Kernel C
Selected original syscall/helper bodies plus
reviewed dependency-model C; not the whole kernel.
Application C
User-program source compiled into application.elf.
Separate from kernel C and generated runtime C.
Generated C
Replay support: context helpers, codecs, loaders
and adapters; not original application/kernel source.
Application ELF
User executable: application.elf or supplied ELF;
import keeps original.elf and patches patched.elf.
Proof / replay ELF
Proof: kernel slices + runtime + test driver.
Replay: application payload + kernel slices + runtime.
slices.elf name
Used in both proof and composed-image directories.
Its role depends on the stage; neither is a full kernel.
Testing purposes
LiteOS / C frontend
LiteOS validates the kernel-port and replay path.
The C frontend creates controlled application fixtures.
